Measured at Axe 3, though, were -20 to -21%; so hit duration does not follow 1/CombatSpeed exactly, and the test character's Fitness is not in the log. Trait Facts shows the measured -20% and gives the measured condition in the note (Firefighter Axe, Axe 3) and that per code it gets smaller with the Pickaxe and at high Axe and Fitness; until fact sweep 2 (2026-09-23) the note said "for a new character", though only Axe 3 was measured, and gave the -12% at Axe 10 as a fact. Measurements at Axe 2, at Axe 10 with Fitness 10 and with the Pickaxe are still to come.

marksman/hitchance.note: Not measured: the game calculates the hit chance in a method the test mod can neither call nor read from Lua. That leaves the hit rate of real shots, which also depends on recoil, aiming delay and zombie movement. Below 3.5 tiles (POINT_BLANK_DISTANCE) the game divides the whole hit chance, the +20 included, by distance/3.5 x 1.1 (CombatManager lines 2228-2231); up close the bonus counts for more, though the chance is usually at 100 there anyway.

Share of poisonings over all runs: without 0.407, with Iron Gut 0.195. Factors of the single runs: 0.4136, 0.4518, 0.5236, 0.4590, 0.5495, 0.5048, 0.4703, 0.4564. The counted events are heavy doses: spoiled food always poisons, and the roll only picks between 5 x and 2 x (hunger x 10 x portion). The effective factor is min(b/2, 100) / min(b, 100): x0.5 only up to a base of 100, less above it, none from 200. For the 205 foods with a 2-day span (for example cabbage, opened cans) that point comes 4 days after they rot; an apple (span 3) is still at x0.83 at the 5-day cap. The measurement (rotten apples, base about 40%) sits where x0.5 applies in full. The note says so since fact sweep 3 (2026-09-23). Since fact sweep 3 (2026-09-23) the English row says "rotten" instead of "spoiled", as the game does (Tooltip_food_Rotten); stale food never takes this branch.

speeddemon/topspeed.note: Measured on 2026-09-10 in the plateau test, factor with/without: SmallCar 1.1162, StepVan 1.1133, CarNormal 1.1120, PickUpVan 1.1115 and 1.1102. The third PickUpVan pair is excluded: in that phase the car reached only 40.341 km/h instead of 88.918, so the plateau was not reached. The log does not give the cause. With that pair the log reports 0.9084. Confirmed on 2026-09-11 from standstill: PickUpVan 79.925 to 88.893 km/h, factor 1.1122. CarNormal sits at the cap of 122.400 km/h with the trait, so its factor is limited by the cap. SportsCar already drives 122.400 km/h without the trait, factor 1.0000. Why about +11% and not +15%: the 1.15 only moves the point where engine force starts to drop. Force is zero at maxSpeed x 1.15 + 20 km/h, without the trait at maxSpeed + 20 km/h. On the PickUpVan (maxSpeed 60.0) that is 89.0 against 80.0 km/h. In multiplayer, also when hosting, the client computes with an inflated speed (CarController lines 130-136, a factor up to 120 / speed limit) and cuts engine force at the real speed limit (lines 681-683, default 70). By the plateau rule ordinary cars gain about 5 to 7% there and fast ones nothing; computed only, not measured in multiplayer. The note says so since fact sweep 3 (2026-09-23); before, it said "servers cap at 70 km/h by default", which is the real speed, while the gauge shows 120 there.

kletterwert-eins.title: A climbing score of 1 to 3 always fails at tall fences, worse than 0 (without a heavy load)
kletterwert-eins.consequence: At tall fences the game rolls 1 in the root of the climbing score. At root 1 (a sum of 1 to 3) Rand.NextBool(1) is always true, so the character fails every time. At root 0, though, without a heavy load it succeeds with Rand.Next(100) <= max(1, Strength), 6 times in 100 at Strength 5 (never with a heavy load). Pathfinding routes over tall fences from a score of 1, so it sends the character to fences where it always fails. This hits for example a new character without gloves with High Weight (Fitness 4, 18 - 15 = 3; gloves add 4) or Clumsy with High Weight. From the code, not measured in play. Not with the sandbox option Easy Climbing (on in the Rising preset): then every climb succeeds without a roll (ClimbOverWallState lines 292-294).

tests.name: Axe: Ax-pert
tests.measures: How fast Ax-pert chops trees, how much damage it does to them and how fast it swings.
tests.how: The test mod fells a tree with and without the trait, then times swings into the air.

tests.name: Adrenaline: speed under panic
tests.measures: Whether Adrenaline Junkie makes you walk, run and sprint faster while panicking.
tests.how: The character moves outdoors while the test mod holds panic at a fixed level and switches the trait on and off. The distance covered is compared.

tests.name: Climbing
tests.measures: The climbing score, which decides how often you fail to climb a tall fence, and the climbing speed on sheet ropes, for Fitness, Strength and Nimble at every level, and for traits like Clumsy, Gymnast or the weight traits. It reads the game's numbers; it does not make the character climb or fall.
tests.how: The test mod steps each skill from 0 to 10 and compares the game's numbers with the formula.

tests.name: New character
tests.measures: Carry capacity and the fitness and strength traits a new character ends up with.
tests.how: Seven characters are created with different traits, and the test mod reads each one right after the start.

tests.name: Code values
tests.measures: About 100 values that can be read directly on a character, such as panic, hit force, wound healing, action times or illness.
tests.how: The test mod adds a trait, reads the value, removes the trait and reads it again. Values that change slowly are sampled over time.

tests.name: Panic outdoors
tests.measures: How fast Agoraphobic builds up panic outside.
tests.how: The character stands outdoors while the test mod switches the trait on and off and measures panic per second.

tests.key: Blut und Lärm: Blutpanik, Blutstress, Geräusche
tests.name: Blood and noise
tests.measures: Panic and stress from blood with Fear of Blood, and whether Deaf removes stress from noise.
tests.how: The test mod makes the character bleed, hands it bloody axes and plays loud sounds, each with and without the trait.

tests.name: Awake: tiredness, thirst, hunger
tests.measures: How fast traits like Wakeful, High Thirst or Light Eater change tiredness, thirst and hunger.
tests.how: The character stands still for a few in-game hours while the traits take turns. Each phase is compared with the ones around it.

tests.name: Sleep
tests.measures: How long you sleep, how fast you fall asleep and how fast you recover, for Restless Sleeper, Wakeful, Sleepyhead and Night Owl.
tests.how: The character lies down, and the test mod runs the game's sleep code hundreds of times per trait.

tests.name: Fade-in: Eagle Eyed, Short Sighted
tests.measures: How fast zombies fade into view.
tests.how: The test mod places a harmless zombie nearby, hides it again and again and measures how fast it comes back.

tests.name: Running: endurance loss
tests.measures: How fast endurance drops while running with High Weight, Athletic or Short of Breath.
tests.how: The character runs while the test mod refills endurance all the time and measures each drop.

tests.name: In the car: claustrophobia and hotwiring
tests.measures: Claustrophobic's panic in a car, and which skills or traits allow hotwiring.
tests.how: Panic is measured like outdoors. For hotwiring, the test mod checks which option the game's menu would offer.

tests.name: World entry
tests.measures: The readable effects of every trait in one pass, including foraging, XP and bag capacity.
tests.how: Runs by itself when a character enters the world. Each trait is added and removed in turn.

tests.name: Sprint
tests.measures: Whether Athletic and Unfit change sprint speed.
tests.how: The character sprints outdoors while the traits take turns, and the distance per step is compared.

tests.name: Cars
tests.measures: How Speed Demon and Sunday Driver change top speed and acceleration, in five different cars.
tests.how: The character drives at full throttle while the traits take turns. Top speed and pulling force are compared.

tests.name: XP ladder
tests.measures: XP gain per skill at every skill level and every boost level, without any trait. Fast Learner and Slow Learner are not part of this test. They were measured in the world entry runs.
tests.how: The test mod adds XP to a character and reads back what arrives.

tests.name: Level traits
tests.measures: Which fitness and strength trait, like Fit or Weak, the game gives at each skill level.
tests.how: The test mod raises each skill from 0 to 10 and notes the trait the game assigns.

tests.name: Character creation
tests.measures: Which level traits a new character really gets, compared with what Trait Facts predicts.
tests.how: Eleven trait combinations are applied to a test character the way the game does at creation.

tests.name: Patch day run
tests.measures: All automatic tests in one go, to see whether a game update changed anything.
tests.how: One click runs them one after another and lists anything that differs.

why: Some effects only exist on a character standing in the world, like carry capacity or hearing range. A separate test mod loads a throwaway save, turns each trait on and off and reads the values. It is a development tool and not part of the mod.
